source: lib/editorials/vitamin-d-how-much.ts (the site's article of the same title)

lines.text: Vitamin D is the supplement almost everyone is told to take. But how much, which form, and who is actually low? Here are the plain answers.
lines.say: Vitamin D is the supplement almost everyone is told to take. But how much, which form, and who is actually low? Here are the plain answers.

lines.text: The short answer. For most adults in the UK, 10 micrograms a day, which is 400 IU, from October to March. And all year if you get little sun, cover your skin, or have dark skin.
lines.say: The short answer. For most adults in the U K, ten micrograms a day, which is four hundred I U, from October to March. And all year if you get little sun, cover your skin, or have dark skin.

lines.text: Why only winter? Your skin makes vitamin D from sunlight, but in the UK the sun is only strong enough from about April to the end of September.
lines.say: Why only winter? Your skin makes vitamin D from sunlight, but in the U K the sun is only strong enough from about April to the end of September.

lines.text: American advice is a little higher: 600 IU a day, or 800 over 70. Either is a reasonable, safe daily amount.
lines.say: American advice is a little higher: six hundred I U a day, or eight hundred over seventy. Either is a reasonable, safe daily amount.

lines.text: Now the unit trap. 1 microgram is 40 IU. So 10 micrograms is 400 IU, and 25 is 1,000. Mixing them up is the most common way people take far more than they meant to.
lines.say: Now the unit trap. One microgram is forty I U. So ten micrograms is four hundred I U, and twenty-five is a thousand. Mixing them up is the most common way people take far more than they meant to.

lines.text: Is more better? No. In a trial of nearly 26,000 healthy adults, 2,000 IU a day for five years did not reduce cancer, heart attacks or strokes.
lines.say: Is more better? No. In a trial of nearly twenty-six thousand healthy adults, two thousand I U a day for five years did not reduce cancer, heart attacks or strokes.

lines.text: The upper limit for adults is 100 micrograms, or 4,000 IU, a day. Too much for too long raises calcium in the blood, which can harm bones, kidneys and the heart.
lines.say: The upper limit for adults is one hundred micrograms, or four thousand I U, a day. Too much for too long raises calcium in the blood, which can harm bones, kidneys and the heart.

lines.text: Which form? A plain vitamin D3 is all most people need. D2 works as a daily dose too, and suits vegans, as does D3 made from lichen.
lines.say: Which form? A plain vitamin D three is all most people need. D two works as a daily dose too, and suits vegans, as does D three made from lichen.

lines.text: You do not need vitamin K2 with it. And skip high strength tubs unless a doctor advises one.
lines.say: You do not need vitamin K two with it. And skip high strength tubs unless a doctor advises one.

lines.text: Take it with a meal, at any time of day. Consistency matters more than timing.
lines.say: Take it with a meal, at any time of day. Consistency matters more than timing.

lines.text: Who is low? About one in five UK adults across the year, and more in winter.
lines.say: Who is low? About one in five U K adults across the year, and more in winter.

lines.text: Skin colour makes the biggest difference. In one large UK study, 57% of people of South Asian ancestry were deficient in winter and spring.
lines.say: Skin colour makes the biggest difference. In one large U K study, fifty-seven percent of people of South Asian ancestry were deficient in winter and spring.

lines.text: Also at risk: people who are rarely outdoors, people who cover their skin, older people, and breastfed babies.
lines.say: Also at risk: people who are rarely outdoors, people who cover their skin, older people, and breastfed babies.

lines.text: Do you need a blood test first? No. For the standard dose, testing does not change the advice.
lines.say: Do you need a blood test first? No. For the standard dose, testing does not change the advice.

lines.text: Check with a doctor or pharmacist first if you have kidney disease, a condition that affects calcium, or take certain medicines, such as some diuretics or steroids.
lines.say: Check with a doctor or pharmacist first if you have kidney disease, a condition that affects calcium, or take certain medicines, such as some diuretics or steroids.

lines.text: So. 10 micrograms a day through the darker months. Plain D3. Check the units, and stay under 100 micrograms. This is general information, not medical advice. The full guide is at sharpandlean.com.
lines.say: So. Ten micrograms a day through the darker months. Plain D three. Check the units, and stay under one hundred micrograms. This is general information, not medical advice. The full guide is at sharp and lean dot com.
